PullRequest.Title: ci: skip core test jobs that the changes cannot affect
PullRequest.Body:
The core PR test jobs run for every pull request, even when the changes cannot affect them: a README edit, a Rust change in `cli/`, or a change confined to the Copilot extension still runs about 270 runner-minutes of core tests. This PR lets those jobs skip, building on the `Detect Changes` job from #342091, and keeps every required check name unchanged.

## Why a reporter job

The required checks are named `<OS> / Electron-Unit`, `Electron`, `Electron-Smoke`, `Browser` and `Remote`. The reusable test workflows name their single job `${{ inputs.job_name }}`, and GitHub does not evaluate the name of a skipped job (the cause of #342134), so these jobs cannot skip under their required names. Instead:

- **The test jobs are renamed** to `<OS> (run) / <job>`, `<OS> (unit) / Browser`, `<OS> (integration & smoke) / Browser` and `<OS> (shard n/2) / Electron-Smoke`, and skip with a job-level `if:` in the calling job. The reusable workflows are unchanged.
- **A `required-checks` job reports the 15 required checks.** It replaces `electron-smoke-checks` and `browser-checks`, which already used this pattern. A check passes when each of its jobs succeeded, or was skipped while change detection succeeded and said the changes cannot affect it. Any other result fails the check, including an unexpected skip, failed detection or a missing output.
- **Browser parts are separate jobs** instead of a matrix, because a job-level `if:` cannot depend on the matrix and the two parts skip under different rules.

## What skips

`detect-changes` gets three outputs. Each is `false` only when **every** changed file is one those tests cannot read; any other path, including a new kind of file, runs the jobs.

| Output | Jobs | Skips when every change is |
|---|---|---|
| `unit-tests` | Electron-Unit, Browser (unit) | docs, `cli/`, `copilot_shim/`, or a built-in extension the unit tests do not read |
| `browser-integration` | Browser (integration & smoke) | docs, `cli/`, `copilot_shim/`, or `extensions/copilot/` |
| `product-tests` | Electron, Electron-Smoke, Remote | docs, `cli/` or `copilot_shim/` |

- **Docs** means Markdown outside `src/`, `test/` and `extensions/`, which use Markdown files as test inputs.
- **Extensions read by unit tests:** the component fixtures load the `theme-*` extensions and the `css`, `html`, `javascript`, `json` and `typescript-basics` grammars, so changes there still run the unit tests. A test fails when a core test starts reading another extension.
- **Copilot:** the Electron integration tests (`copilot` suite) and the Electron and remote smoke tests load the Copilot extension, so they keep running for Copilot changes.
- **Fail-open:** as before, every job runs when the changed-file lookup fails, is incomplete, or returns no files.

## Expected impact

Based on the 744 PRs merged Oct 9–19 and average job times from 25 recent successful runs:

| PR type | Share | Saved per run |
|---|---|---|
| Copilot extension only | 6.3% | ~108 runner-min (Electron-Unit, Browser unit and integration & smoke) |
| Other built-in extension only | 1.9% | ~81 runner-min (Electron-Unit, Browser unit) |
| Docs, `cli/` or `copilot_shim/` only | 1.1% | ~272 runner-min (all core test jobs) |

Across all PRs that is about 11 runner-minutes per run (~4%), about 4.4 of them on the Windows 1ES pool. It frees capacity rather than shortening runs, because `Windows / Electron` stays the longest job. More importantly, this sets up the reporter that later rules need, such as skipping unit test jobs based on which tests the changes import.

## Trade-offs

- **The test jobs start after `Detect Changes`**, which finishes 10–15 seconds into the run.
- **The 15 required checks report together** when the last test job finishes, instead of one by one. The renamed test jobs still report as soon as they finish.

## How to test

- **This PR** edits `pr.yml`, so every job runs and every required check should pass through `required-checks`.
- **Already run:**
  - `node --test lib/test/detectChanges.test.ts` in `build/`: rule table, renames, fail-open behavior, the extension scan and the `pr.yml` wiring. I confirmed the tests fail when an extension the tests read is made skippable, and when a test job reports a required name itself.
  - The `required-checks` script against 8 simulated `needs` results: success, intended skips, an unexpected skip, failed detection, a missing output, a failure and a cancellation.
  - A docs-only pull request in a fork, based on this change ([run](https://github.com/bryanchen-d/vscode/actions/runs/39336962178)): `Detect Changes` reported all three outputs as `false`, every core test job was skipped, and all 15 required checks reported success under their exact names.
  - `actionlint` on `pr.yml`: no new findings compared with `main`. `npm run eslint` and a strict `tsc --noEmit` on the changed TypeScript passed.
- **After merge:** the first Copilot-only PR should show the Electron-Unit and Browser test jobs as skipped and every required check as passing.

> Authored with Copilot

Scenarios.Scenario: Core/source pull request running the full cross-platform test matrix
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The diff moves all 21 expanded core test jobs behind Detect Changes; its sparse checkout and changed-file API pagination must now finish before those jobs can be scheduled. The 15 required-check reporter jobs then wait for every core test job, so merge readiness includes one small reporter execution after the slowest test. Test execution itself remains the dominant critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Sparse checkout of the detector plus GitHub pull-request changed-file pagination
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sparse checkout and ceil(changed-file-count/100) API pages per workflow run, shared by every path rule
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Detect Changes already performed the same checkout and API pagination for CLI/Copilot selection, but core test jobs did not depend on it and could schedule immediately.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This existing detection work is newly placed before every core test job, adding its bounded 10–15 second-scale gate to otherwise full test runs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reusable test workflows perform checkout, cache restore, dependency/download setup, and test-specific external setup
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: 21 expanded jobs for a core-affecting PR: seven per OS including two smoke shards
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same 21 expanded test jobs ran concurrently without waiting for Detect Changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These boundaries dominate CI duration; their count and internal behavior are unchanged for a core-affecting pull request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Schedule and execute required-check reporter jobs that parse bounded needs metadata with jq
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: 15 short reporter jobs; previously six reporter jobs covered Browser and Electron-Smoke while nine test jobs reported required names directly
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Electron-Unit, Electron, and Remote required checks completed directly with their test jobs; Browser and Electron-Smoke used six reporter jobs grouped by category.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All reporters wait for the full matrix and add one bounded runner/job hop after the slowest test before all required names settle.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Changed-file pagination scales by one request per 100 files; full test cardinality is fixed at 21 expanded jobs and reporter cardinality at 15 checks.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: After the single Detect Changes job completes, the same 21 expanded test jobs can run independently across Linux, macOS, and Windows; smoke tests remain two shards per OS. The reporter expands to 15 independent Ubuntu jobs only after all 18 calling-job IDs (21 matrix-expanded jobs) settle.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Detector results are computed once and shared as job outputs; failures, empty lists, and incomplete lists fail open to full tests. Existing dependency and built-in-extension caches inside reusable workflows are unchanged for both warm and cold runs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new needs edges, fixed matrix cardinalities, API pagination, and reporter fan-in are explicit in the workflow.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runner queue time and reporter startup duration vary, but the added gate and reporter hop are bounded and small relative to the unchanged full test matrix.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The bounded latency overhead is an intentional scheduling tradeoff required to eliminate much larger test work on unaffected pull requests, and no concrete unbounded or multiplicative mechanism was introduced on full runs.

Scenarios.Scenario: Documentation-, cli/-, or copilot_shim/-only pull request
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Detect Changes is the only prerequisite for core checks. Once it classifies every path as skippable, all 21 expanded core test jobs are omitted and 15 short reporter jobs establish the required check names.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Sparse checkout and changed-file API pagination
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sparse checkout plus ceil(changed-file-count/100) API pages
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The detector already ran for other path-filtered jobs, but its result did not suppress core tests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to prove all changed paths are skippable; it replaces the much longer test critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Core test job scheduling and execution
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero after the diff versus 21 expanded test jobs before the diff
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All Electron unit/integration/smoke, browser unit/integration/smoke, and remote jobs ran regardless of these changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The expensive cross-platform test boundaries are removed entirely for this scenario.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: 15 short jobs after detection versus six reporters plus 21 full tests previously
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Six Browser/Smoke reporters ran only after their full tests, while other required names came directly from full test jobs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reporter provisioning is the remaining bounded post-detection work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Classification scans each changed and previous rename path against three core rules; realistic cardinality is the GitHub changed-file list, with early find termination per rule.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One detector runs first; no core test runner is provisioned. Fifteen bounded reporter jobs may then run concurrently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no persistent detector cache; one computed output set is coalesced across all jobs. Lookup failure, truncation, or an empty list disables skipping rather than repeatedly retrying.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: job-level conditions consume the three detector outputs and omit every core job when all paths are skippable.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact runner-minute savings depend on cache warmth and queue time, but removal of 21 heavyweight jobs is mechanically certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Performance improvement, not a regression. The diff replaces large fixed CI fan-out with one existing detector and bounded reporters.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Detect Changes classifies unit and browser integration groups as unaffected while product tests remain required because Electron and remote scenarios load Copilot. Product tests and their reporters remain on the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Changed-file API pagination and sparse detector checkout
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The detector ran for Copilot jobs but did not gate core tests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Gates both skipped and retained groups before scheduling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Product test workflow checkouts, cache restores, setup downloads, and tests
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: 12 expanded jobs remain; nine expanded unit/browser jobs are removed
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Unchanged product-test work remains critical; removed groups no longer consume runners or boundaries.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed cross-platform matrix cardinality after one path classification; no per-file test invocation is introduced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Nine expanded unit/browser jobs are skipped; 12 expanded product jobs (Electron integration, two smoke shards, and Remote per OS) can run concurrently after detection. Fifteen reporters wait for the settled matrix.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing node_modules, built-in-extension, Electron, and tool caches remain per job. Detection is shared and fail-open; no repeated cache misses are introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the rule table and workflow conditions directly establish which groups skip.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual savings vary with runner and dependency cache hits, but nine omitted heavyweight jobs are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Performance improvement with unchanged concurrency for retained product tests; no regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Compile & Hygiene running the newly added detector tests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: test-build-scripts runs alongside the other Compile & Hygiene commands. The new test performs one synchronous git grep and then reads only matching candidate source files before validating extension coverage.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run git grep over src/**/test/** and test/unit/** to find extension-path references
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one git subprocess per test-build-scripts invocation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No detector test or extension-reference scan ran.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Can extend the build-test branch of Compile & Hygiene, but it is a bounded repository-indexed scan and is concurrent with other compile checks.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read each grep candidate and check referenced extension paths
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per JavaScript/TypeScript grep match plus bounded existence checks; candidates are narrowed before reading
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No corresponding file reads were performed by this test suite.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local filesystem work inside one test; no repeated per-rule repository scan.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The subprocess scans test-tree tracked files once; subsequent work scales with files containing an extensions/<name>/ reference, not all repository files.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The build test process runs in parallel with the other npm-run-all tasks, but its internal git subprocess and candidate file reads are serial and single-shot.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is added; git's index/object cache and OS filesystem cache determine warm behavior. The scan is not repeated within the suite.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added subprocess and reads; low evidence of material latency because there is no multiplication across test cases or core test jobs.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact candidate count and disk timing were not measured, but the narrowing, one-shot invocation, and limited test directories bound the mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The test adds bounded validation work once in the dedicated build-script suite, with no realistic fan-out or unbounded allocation.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and all diff pages. Traced CI scheduling, GitHub API pagination, reusable test fan-out, reporter synchronization, cache behavior, and the new build-test subprocess/filesystem scan. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
